subdomain: 1.4 Design multi-agent systems and orchestration strategies

en.question: A scheduling prototype assigns one agent per depot. Each allocation changes a shared vehicle pool, so nearly every decision invalidates another worker's assumptions. Broadcasting all intermediate state consumes the savings from parallel work, and independent full-plan attempts exceed the cost budget. Which redesign addresses the task's dependency structure?

options.text: Use one authoritative planner for interdependent allocations and delegate only checks that have stable, separable inputs.
options.note: A single owner of coupled allocation state avoids continual reconciliation between conflicting plans. Separate workers remain useful only where their inputs and responsibilities are genuinely independent.

options.text: Add a worker for each vehicle and broadcast its proposed location after every allocation to all depot agents.
options.note: Finer partitioning increases the participants that must coordinate around the same shared resource. It does not remove the dependency causing invalidated assumptions.

options.text: Let depot agents finish independently and ask a synthesis agent to combine their plans without revisiting the allocation decisions.
options.note: Independently valid depot plans can assign the same vehicle simultaneously. Prose synthesis cannot guarantee a valid shared allocation without solving the coupled decisions again.

options.text: Have every worker construct a complete global schedule and choose the most popular final plan by voting.
options.note: Full-plan duplication is explicitly outside the cost budget. Voting also changes the task from coordinating allocations to repeating the entire search.
